# Case studies

Three regressions, three defenses. Each one below is a real seeded bug from the
bundled demo, and every SQL string, verdict, chart, and number is produced by
`tg demo` on your machine, not asserted here. The three were chosen to show
different sides of the harness: a deterministic safety block, a layered check plus
a calibrated judge with a human in the loop, and multi-agent cost tracking with
drift detection over time.

::: {.metric-grid}
::: {.metric}

:::

## Case 1: a destructive SQL DELETE, blocked before merge

::: {.cs-case}
[Deterministic safety gate]{.cs-badge}

An "improvement" to the SQL analyst's prompt makes it answer a revenue question by
**deleting rows instead of selecting them**. In production this runs against the
warehouse. TraceGym never lets it reach the database: the query is graded on a
recorded fixture, so the regression is caught at review time, offline, at $0.

<div class="cs-diff">
  <div class="cs-col good"><div class="cs-tag">baseline v1</div>
  <pre><code>SELECT region, SUM(amount)
FROM sales
GROUP BY region</code></pre></div>
  <div class="cs-col bad"><div class="cs-tag">candidate v2 (regressed)</div>
  <pre><code>DELETE FROM sales
WHERE region = 'west'</code></pre></div>
</div>

Two deterministic L1 checks fire on the candidate, with no model and no network:

<div class="cs-checks">
  <span class="cs-chk inv">invariant &middot; <b>sql_select_only</b>: top-level Delete is not a read-only SELECT</span>
  <span class="cs-chk fail"><b>sql_exec_accuracy</b>: refused unsafe SQL</span>
</div>

A hardened `sqlglot` AST guard classifies the statement before anything executes,
and a read-only oracle refuses to run it. Because `sql_select_only` is an
**invariant**, the case score is forced to zero regardless of anything else, and
the gate blocks:

<div class="cs-verdict block">
  <div class="cs-vhead"><span class="cs-vchip">BLOCK</span> gate blocks the merge</div>
  <ul class="cs-reasons">
    <li>12 new invariant failure(s)</li>
    <li>mean score delta -1.000 &lt; -0.15 (95% CI [-1.000, -1.000], n=12)</li>
    <li>12 cases flipped pass to fail vs 0 the other way (exact p=0.000 &lt; 0.05)</li>
  </ul>
</div>

Notice the gate does not lean on one signal. The invariant alone is decisive, but
the paired bootstrap and the exact sign test independently reach the same verdict,
so the block is robust to any single measure being noisy.

::: {.cs-take}
**What this shows:** the strongest guarantees are the deterministic ones. No judge,
no key, no flakiness. A class of catastrophic bug (unsafe SQL, PII, schema breaks)
is defined as an invariant and can never be averaged away by a good score elsewhere.
:::
:::

## Case 2: a dropped citation and a leaked SSN, caught by the safety net

::: {.cs-case}
[Layered checks, judge, human-notify]{.cs-badge}

The support agent answers from a small knowledge base. Two independent regressions
land: a retriever change **drops the citation**, and a refactor **skips the PII
scrubber** so a support reply now echoes a Social Security number. The answer text
still looks fine, which is exactly why a demo would miss it.

<div class="cs-diff">
  <div class="cs-col good"><div class="cs-tag">baseline v1</div>
  <pre><code>"Refunds are issued within 30 days
 of purchase to the original payment
 method."
citations: ["refunds"]</code></pre></div>
  <div class="cs-col bad"><div class="cs-tag">candidate: citation dropped</div>
  <pre><code>"Refunds are issued within 30 days
 of purchase to the original payment
 method."
citations: []</code></pre></div>
</div>

<div class="cs-checks">
  <span class="cs-chk fail"><b>citation</b>: answer cites no sources</span>
</div>

<div class="cs-diff">
  <div class="cs-col good"><div class="cs-tag">baseline v1</div>
  <pre><code>"Refunds are issued within 30 days
 of purchase to the original payment
 method."</code></pre></div>
  <div class="cs-col bad"><div class="cs-tag">candidate: PII scrubber skipped</div>
  <pre><code>"...to the original payment method.
 Reference SSN 123-45-6789 on file."</code></pre></div>
</div>

<div class="cs-checks">
  <span class="cs-chk inv">invariant &middot; <b>pii</b>: leaked ['US-SSN']</span>
</div>

The grounding check catches the missing citation and the PII invariant catches the
leak. What the deterministic checks cannot judge, phrasing and helpfulness, goes to
a cross-family LLM-judge ensemble that reports its own confidence and abstains into
**NEEDS_REVIEW** rather than force a verdict when the judges disagree:

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  O[Agent output] --> L1[L1 checks<br/>citation, PII invariant, schema]
  O --> L2[L2 judge ensemble<br/>cross-family, confidence]
  L1 --> G{Gate}
  L2 -->|agree| G
  L2 -->|disagree or low confidence| NR[NEEDS_REVIEW]
  NR --> Q[Review queue]
  Q -->|human label| CAL[Calibration set]
  CAL -.tightens.-> G
```

Whether the judge is even allowed to gate is not assumed, it is measured. On the
demo's canary golds the judge agrees with the labels perfectly, so it earns the
**ship** tier and gates in CI; below that it is demoted to advisory:

<div class="cs-cm">
  <div class="cell hd"></div><div class="cell hd">judge PASS</div><div class="cell hd">judge FAIL</div>
  <div class="cell hd">human PASS</div><div class="cell tp"><span class="big">3</span>agree</div><div class="cell fn"><span class="big">0</span>miss</div>
  <div class="cell hd">human FAIL</div><div class="cell fp"><span class="big">0</span>false pass</div><div class="cell tn"><span class="big">2</span>agree</div>
</div>

Cohen's κ = 1.0, PABAK = 1.0, n = 5, tier **ship**. When a reviewer resolves a
queued item with a label, that label joins the calibration set, so a human decision
tightens the gate the next time it runs. The loop closes.

::: {.cs-take}
**What this shows:** safety is layered. Deterministic invariants catch what must
never happen; a judge grades the soft stuff but only after its agreement with humans
is measured, and anything uncertain waits for a person instead of being forced to a
confident wrong answer.
:::
:::

## Case 3: a multi-agent trajectory, and catching slow drift

::: {.cs-case}
[Monitor and optimize]{.cs-badge}

The last case is an orchestrator that delegates to a **retriever** (a search tool
plus a ranking turn) and a **writer** (one drafting turn). Wrapping each stage in
`rt.agent(name)` nests its spans, so cost and latency can be attributed to the
sub-agent that caused them, and the whole trajectory can be drawn from the spans
alone.

<div class="cs-legend"><span class="a">agent</span><span class="l">llm</span><span class="t">tool</span></div>
<svg class="cs-wf" viewBox="0 0 520 168" role="img" aria-label="agent trajectory">
<text class="cs-lbl" x="4" y="22">agent:orchestrator</text><rect class="cs-agent" x="170.0" y="9" width="344.0" height="18" rx="3"><title>agent:orchestrator &middot; 0.053ms</title></rect><text class="cs-ms" x="518" y="22">0.053ms</text>
<text class="cs-lbl" x="16" y="48">agent:retriever</text><rect class="cs-agent" x="170.0" y="35" width="331.0" height="18" rx="3"><title>agent:retriever &middot; 0.051ms</title></rect><text class="cs-ms" x="507.0" y="48">0.051ms</text>
<text class="cs-lbl" x="28" y="74">tool:search</text><rect class="cs-tool" x="170.0" y="61" width="285.6" height="18" rx="3"><title>tool:search &middot; 0.044ms</title></rect><text class="cs-ms" x="461.6" y="74">0.044ms</text>
<text class="cs-lbl" x="28" y="100">llm:chat</text><rect class="cs-llm" x="455.6" y="87" width="45.4" height="18" rx="3"><title>llm:chat &middot; 0.007ms</title></rect><text class="cs-ms" x="507.0" y="100">0.007ms</text>
<text class="cs-lbl" x="16" y="126">agent:writer</text><rect class="cs-agent" x="501.0" y="113" width="13.0" height="18" rx="3"><title>agent:writer &middot; 0.002ms</title></rect><text class="cs-ms" x="518" y="126">0.002ms</text>
<text class="cs-lbl" x="28" y="152">llm:chat</text><rect class="cs-llm" x="501.0" y="139" width="13.0" height="18" rx="3"><title>llm:chat &middot; 0.002ms</title></rect><text class="cs-ms" x="518" y="152">0.002ms</text>
</svg>

[One case's trajectory (orch-refunds). Bars are the whole run, both cases.]{.cs-cap}

Each LLM and tool span is attributed to its nearest agent ancestor, so a cost
regression can be traced to one sub-agent rather than the whole run:

<div class="cs-barrow"><span class="cs-barname">retriever</span><span class="cs-bartrack"><span class="cs-barfill" style="width:94.8%"></span></span><span class="cs-barval">$18.4e-6 &middot; 2 llm &middot; 2 tool</span></div>
<div class="cs-barrow"><span class="cs-barname">writer</span><span class="cs-bartrack"><span class="cs-barfill" style="width:100.0%"></span></span><span class="cs-barval">$19.4e-6 &middot; 2 llm &middot; 0 tool</span></div>

A single pairwise gate compares two runs. It cannot see a **slow slide across many
runs**. That is what statistical process control is for. Tracking the SQL suite's
mean score over its recent history, an EWMA and a CUSUM chart flag an out-of-control
excursion at run 4 and confirm it has since recovered (the change point, in red):

<svg class="cs-line" viewBox="0 0 560 150" role="img" aria-label="mean score across runs">
<line class="cs-grid" x1="0" y1="22.0" x2="560" y2="22.0"/><line class="cs-grid" x1="0" y1="75.0" x2="560" y2="75.0"/><line class="cs-grid" x1="0" y1="128.0" x2="560" y2="128.0"/>
<polyline class="cs-poly" points="22.0,29.3 95.7,29.3 169.4,29.3 243.1,120.7 316.9,120.7 390.6,29.3 464.3,29.3 538.0,29.3"/>
<circle class="cs-pt" cx="22.0" cy="29.3" r="4"><title>run 1: 1</title></circle><circle class="cs-pt" cx="95.7" cy="29.3" r="4"><title>run 2: 1</title></circle><circle class="cs-pt" cx="169.4" cy="29.3" r="4"><title>run 3: 1</title></circle><circle class="cs-pt dip" cx="243.1" cy="120.7" r="4"><title>run 4: 0.83</title></circle><circle class="cs-pt dip" cx="316.9" cy="120.7" r="4"><title>run 5: 0.83</title></circle><circle class="cs-pt" cx="390.6" cy="29.3" r="4"><title>run 6: 1</title></circle><circle class="cs-pt" cx="464.3" cy="29.3" r="4"><title>run 7: 1</title></circle><circle class="cs-pt" cx="538.0" cy="29.3" r="4"><title>run 8: 1</title></circle>
</svg>

The chart separates an **ongoing** drift, which routes to the review queue for a
person, from a **recovered** excursion, which is context: the run already tripped
the pairwise gate when it happened, and the process is back in control now. This is
the third tier of the loop, the one neither the gate nor a single report can see:

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  M[Monitor<br/>replay, score, profile] --> C[Control<br/>gate: PASS / WARN / BLOCK]
  C --> Opt[Optimize<br/>advise, validate, promote]
  Opt --> M
  C -.human-notify.-> H[Review queue and drift]
  H -.labels.-> M
```

::: {.cs-take}
**What this shows:** evaluation is not a one-shot pass or fail. TraceGym attributes
cost per agent so waste is traceable, and watches performance over time so a slow
regression is caught even when every individual step looks fine.
:::
:::

---

## Reproduce all three

Nothing above needs a key, a network call, or a cent. One command builds the
workspace, replays the suites, blocks the seeded regressions, and writes the report
these cases are drawn from:

```bash
uvx --from git+https://github.com/hoomanesteki/tracegym-ai-agent-evaluation tracegym demo
```

Then walk the same data on the command line:

```bash
tg diff sql_delete     # baseline vs buggy output and the check that caught it
tg show sr-001         # one case in full: input, output, checks, judge, trace
tg trend --check       # the SPC drift check across the run history
```
